title: LC Oscillations
short: Energy sloshes between the capacitor and the inductor at ω = 1/√(LC), like a mass on a spring.
trouble: Students think the current is greatest when the capacitor holds the most charge.

blocks.html: Connect a charged capacitor to an inductor, with no resistor and no battery. The capacitor starts to discharge, but the inductor will not let the current stop: when the capacitor is empty, the current keeps going and charges it the other way. Energy sloshes back and forth between the capacitor's electric field and the inductor's magnetic field, exactly the way it moves between a spring and a mass.

Around the loop, the capacitor's voltage equals the inductor's emf: $\dfrac{q}{C} = -L\dfrac{dI}{dt}$, with $I = dq/dt$. So $$L\frac{d^2q}{dt^2} + \frac{q}{C} = 0,$$ the equation of simple harmonic motion with $q$ in place of $x$. Its solution is $q = Q_0\cos\omega t$ with $\omega^2 = \dfrac{1}{LC}$.

$$\omega = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}, \qquad q = Q_0\cos\omega t, \qquad I = -Q_0\omega\sin\omega t.$$
        The total energy $\dfrac{q^2}{2C} + \tfrac{1}{2}LI^2 = \dfrac{Q_0^2}{2C}$ stays constant. The current is largest, $Q_0\omega$, when the capacitor is empty.

blocks.name: ph-circuit
blocks.cap: An LC circuit: the capacitor's voltage and the current are a quarter cycle apart, and the energy bars trade places twice each cycle.

blocks.name: springmass
blocks.cap: The mechanical twin: a mass on a spring with no friction. Position plays the role of charge, velocity the role of current.

blocks.title: Frequency and peak current
blocks.q: A $5.0\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor charged to $10\ \text{V}$ is connected to a $20\ \text{mH}$ inductor. Find the frequency and the largest current.
steps: Check with energy: $\tfrac{1}{2}CV_0^2 = 2.5 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{J}$ and $\tfrac{1}{2}LI_{\max}^2 = 2.50 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{J}$. They match.

blocks.title: Tuning a radio
blocks.q: A tuner uses a $200\ \text{pF}$ capacitor. What inductance makes it resonate at $1.0\ \text{MHz}$, in the AM band?

blocks.html: "The current is greatest when the capacitor holds the most charge." It is the other way around. When the capacitor is fully charged, all the energy is in its electric field and the current is momentarily zero, like a pendulum at the end of its swing. The current peaks a quarter cycle later, when the capacitor is empty and all the energy is in the inductor. Check: $q = Q_0\cos\omega t$ and $I = -Q_0\omega\sin\omega t$ are never largest at the same time.
